questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is commonly represented as calcium oxychloride, CaOCl₂, though commercial material is a mixture; used for bleaching and disinfection.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are the major nutrients supplied by NPK fertilisers?
questions.explanation: Major nutrients supplied by fertilisers include nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (NPK).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a greenhouse gas?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas. Major greenhouse gases include water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, ozone and fluorinated gases.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which chemicals are primarily responsible for ozone-layer depletion?
questions.explanation: Ozone-depleting substances such as chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and halons release chlorine or bromine radicals in the stratosphere that catalytically destroy ozone.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which polymer is used in non-stick coatings?
questions.explanation: Teflon is the trade name commonly used for polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), a chemically resistant, low-friction polymer used in non-stick coatings, seals and industrial applications.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which polymer is used in beverage bottles and textile fibres?
questions.explanation: Polyester is a family of polymers containing ester linkages; PET is widely used in textile fibres and beverage bottles.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What type of bond is formed when sodium loses one electron and chlorine gains one electron?
questions.explanation: Sodium loses one electron to form Na⁺ and chlorine gains one electron to form Cl⁻; electrostatic attraction between the ions forms an ionic lattice (ionic bond).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What type of bond is present in a water molecule (H₂O)?
questions.explanation: Water (H₂O) is a covalent compound; covalent bonds are formed when atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: In a blast furnace, iron is produced from:
questions.explanation: Iron is produced in a blast furnace from iron ore; its oxides can be reduced using carbon or carbon monoxide.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which acid is present in vinegar?
questions.explanation: Dilute aqueous ethanoic acid is the main acid in vinegar.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which functional group is present in ethanol?
questions.explanation: Ethanol is an alcohol containing a hydroxyl group (-OH) bonded to a saturated carbon atom.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which functional group is present in ethanoic acid?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid is a carboxylic acid containing the -COOH functional group.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an antacid?
questions.explanation: Antacids are substances that neutralise excess stomach acid; examples include magnesium hydroxide, aluminium hydroxide and calcium carbonate.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an analgesic?
questions.explanation: Analgesics are medicines that relieve pain; examples include paracetamol and ibuprofen.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: High BOD in water often indicates:
questions.explanation: High BOD often indicates organic pollution because microorganisms use dissolved oxygen to decompose organic matter.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Eutrophication is caused by excess:
questions.explanation: Eutrophication is excess nutrient enrichment, especially by nitrogen and phosphorus, causing algal blooms and oxygen depletion that can harm aquatic life.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the difference between bioaccumulation and biomagnification?

options.A: Bioaccumulation is build-up in one organism; biomagnification is increase at higher trophic levels
options.B: Bioaccumulation is increase at higher trophic levels; biomagnification is build-up in one organism
options.D: Both refer to breakdown of chemicals

questions.explanation: Bioaccumulation is the build-up of a chemical in an organism over time when uptake exceeds elimination; biomagnification is the increase in concentration of a persistent substance at successively higher trophic levels in a food chain.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the relative molecular mass of water approximately?
questions.explanation: Water (H₂O) has a relative molecular mass of approximately 18.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the relative molecular mass of carbon dioxide approximately?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) has a relative molecular mass of approximately 44.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the relative molecular mass of ammonia approximately?
questions.explanation: Ammonia (NH₃) has a relative molecular mass of approximately 17.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the relative molecular mass of methane approximately?
questions.explanation: Methane (CH₄) has a relative molecular mass of approximately 16.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical name of baking soda?
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate (sodium bicarbonate), NaHCO₃.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical name of washing soda?
questions.explanation: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical name of Plaster of Paris?
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO₄·½H₂O.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical name of gypsum?
questions.explanation: Gypsum is calcium sulphate dihydrate, CaSO₄·2H₂O.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a type of coal?
questions.explanation: Coal types include peat, lignite, bituminous coal and anthracite. Petrol, kerosene and diesel are petroleum products.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fossil fuel?
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels are coal, petroleum and natural gas formed from ancient organic matter over geological time. Hydrogen is not a fossil fuel.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is produced during the complete combustion of a hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Complete combustion of hydrocarbons produces carbon dioxide and water.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What poisonous gas can be produced during incomplete combustion?
questions.explanation: Incomplete combustion with insufficient oxygen can produce carbon monoxide, soot and other products; carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which method can remove temporary hardness of water?
questions.explanation: Boiling can remove much of the temporary hardness of water by precipitating insoluble compounds.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which method can remove permanent hardness of water?

options.B: Ion-exchange resins or washing soda treatment

questions.explanation: Permanent hardness is not removed by ordinary boiling; methods include washing soda treatment, ion-exchange resins and reverse osmosis.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What percentage of dry air is oxygen by volume?
questions.explanation: Dry air near sea level contains about 20.95% oxygen by volume (approximately 21%).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What percentage of dry air is nitrogen by volume?
questions.explanation: Dry air near sea level contains about 78.08% nitrogen by volume (approximately 78%).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What percentage of dry air is carbon dioxide by volume?
questions.explanation: Dry air near sea level contains about 0.04% carbon dioxide by volume.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What type of bond holds atoms together in a metallic solid?
questions.explanation: A metallic bond is the attraction between positive metal ion cores and delocalised valence electrons throughout a metallic solid; it helps explain conductivity, malleability and ductility.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following metals does NOT react with water under ordinary conditions?
questions.explanation: Copper, silver and gold do not react with water under ordinary conditions. Sodium and potassium react violently with cold water; calcium reacts less vigorously; magnesium reacts with hot water/steam.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which metal does NOT liberate hydrogen from dilute HCl?
questions.explanation: Copper does not liberate hydrogen from dilute HCl because it is below hydrogen in the reactivity series.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a thermosetting plastic?
questions.explanation: Thermosetting plastics form cross-linked networks and do not melt and remould easily after curing; Bakelite is a common example. Thermoplastics such as polyethylene, PVC and polypropylene soften on heating and can generally be remoulded.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a thermoplastic?
questions.explanation: Thermoplastics soften on heating and can generally be remoulded; polyethylene is a thermoplastic. Thermosetting plastics such as Bakelite form cross-linked networks and do not melt and remould easily.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a natural polymer?
questions.explanation: Natural polymers are polymers found in nature, such as cellulose, starch, proteins, natural rubber and DNA.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What type of salts are soaps?

options.A: Sodium or potassium salts of long-chain fatty acids
options.B: Calcium salts of long-chain fatty acids
options.C: Magnesium salts of long-chain fatty acids
options.D: Ammonium salts of long-chain fatty acids

questions.explanation: Soaps are sodium or potassium salts of long-chain fatty acids, produced by saponification of fats or oils with alkali.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What are micelles?

options.A: Aggregates of soap molecules that help disperse oily dirt in water
options.C: Insoluble scum formed in hard water

questions.explanation: Soap molecules have a hydrophilic ionic head and a hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail; they form micelles that help disperse oily dirt in water.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which stage of municipal water treatment involves removing large debris?
questions.explanation: Common stages in municipal drinking-water treatment include screening, coagulation/flocculation, sedimentation, filtration and disinfection.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which stage of municipal water treatment kills disease-causing microorganisms?
questions.explanation: Disinfection is the stage that inactivates many disease-causing microorganisms; chlorination is a common disinfection method.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which gas is colourless and odourless and interferes with oxygen transport by haemoglobin?
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide is colourless and odourless and interferes with oxygen transport by haemoglobin; it binds strongly to haemoglobin to form carboxyhaemoglobin.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which international treaty was adopted in 1987 to phase out ozone-depleting substances?
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol is an international treaty adopted in 1987 to phase out production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances; it is widely regarded as a major environmental agreement.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a pure substance?
questions.explanation: Water is a pure substance (a compound). Air, salt solution and sea water are mixtures. Elements and compounds are pure substances.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a heterogeneous mixture?
questions.explanation: A heterogeneous mixture has a composition that is not uniform throughout, such as sand in water or oil and water.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a homogeneous mixture?
questions.explanation: A homogeneous mixture has uniform composition and properties throughout, such as salt solution or air.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which separation technique is used to separate an insoluble solid from a liquid?
questions.explanation: Filtration is a separation method in which an insoluble solid is retained by a porous filter while the fluid passes through.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which separation technique is based on differences in boiling points or volatility?
questions.explanation: Distillation is a separation or purification method based on differences in boiling points or volatility; the vapour is condensed and collected.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which separation technique is based on different rates of movement of components between a stationary phase and a mobile phase?
questions.explanation: Chromatography is a separation technique based on different rates of movement of components between a stationary phase and a mobile phase; it is used to separate dyes, pigments and mixtures.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which separation technique is used to purify a solid by forming crystals from a suitable solution?
questions.explanation: Crystallisation is the purification of a solid by forming crystals from a suitable solution; impurities tend to remain in the mother liquor.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which group of the periodic table contains noble gases?
questions.explanation: Noble gases are Group 18 elements with very low chemical reactivity because their outer electron shells are filled.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a metalloid?
questions.explanation: Metalloids have properties intermediate between metals and non-metals; commonly listed examples include boron, silicon, germanium, arsenic, antimony and tellurium.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a noble gas?
questions.explanation: Argon is a noble gas. Noble gases include helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which type of bond is formed by sharing one pair of electrons?
questions.explanation: A single covalent bond is formed by sharing one pair of electrons, such as the H–H bond in H₂.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which type of bond is formed by sharing two pairs of electrons?
questions.explanation: A double covalent bond is formed by sharing two pairs of electrons, such as the O=O bond in O₂.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which type of bond is formed by sharing three pairs of electrons?
questions.explanation: A triple covalent bond is formed by sharing three pairs of electrons, such as the N≡N bond in nitrogen gas.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which type of reaction is 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO?
questions.explanation: A combination reaction is a reaction in which two or more reactants form a single product; 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO is an example.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which type of reaction is CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ on heating?
questions.explanation: A decomposition reaction is a reaction in which one compound breaks into two or more simpler substances; CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ on heating is an example.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which type of reaction is Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu?
questions.explanation: A displacement reaction is a reaction in which a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound; Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu is an example.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which type of reaction is AgNO₃ + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO₃?
questions.explanation: A double displacement reaction is a reaction in which ions of two compounds exchange partners; AgNO₃ + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO₃ is an example.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which alloy is mainly composed of copper and zinc?
questions.explanation: Brass is an alloy mainly of copper and zinc. Bronze is mainly copper and tin.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which alloy is mainly composed of copper and tin?
questions.explanation: Bronze is a traditional alloy mainly of copper and tin. Brass is mainly copper and zinc.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which alloy is primarily composed of iron and carbon?
questions.explanation: Steel is an alloy primarily of iron and carbon; other elements may be added to alter its properties.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which carbon allotrope is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice?
questions.explanation: Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice; it has high electrical and thermal conductivity and high mechanical strength.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which carbon allotrope has a hollow cage-like structure?
questions.explanation: Fullerenes are molecular allotropes of carbon made of hollow cage-like structures; C₆₀ is a well-known spherical fullerene.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an antiseptic?
questions.explanation: Antiseptics are chemical agents applied to living tissue to reduce or inhibit microorganisms; examples include appropriately formulated povidone-iodine and chlorhexidine products.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a disinfectant?
questions.explanation: Disinfectants are chemical agents used on inanimate surfaces or objects to destroy or reduce microorganisms; sodium hypochlorite is a common disinfectant. They are not automatically safe for use on skin.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a disinfectant?
questions.explanation: Disinfectants are chemical agents used on inanimate surfaces or objects to destroy or reduce microorganisms; sodium hypochlorite is a common disinfectant. They are not automatically safe for use on skin.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a major air pollutant?
questions.explanation: Major air pollutants include particulate matter (PM₂.₅ and PM₁₀), sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide, ground-level ozone, volatile organic compounds, lead and other toxic substances.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a common water pollutant?
questions.explanation: Common water pollutants include pathogens, sewage, fertilisers, pesticides, industrial chemicals, heavy metals, oil, plastics, sediments and excess nutrients.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an aldehyde?
questions.explanation: An aldehyde is an organic compound containing a terminal -CHO functional group; methanal and ethanal are examples.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a ketone?
questions.explanation: A ketone is an organic compound containing a carbonyl group (>C=O) bonded to two carbon groups; propanone (acetone) is a common example.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the product of esterification between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol?
questions.explanation: Esterification is a reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol, commonly with an acid catalyst, producing an ester and water; esters often have characteristic fruity odours.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an artificial sweetener?
questions.explanation: Artificial sweeteners are sweet-tasting substances used as sugar substitutes, often with little or no energy at the quantities used; examples include saccharin, aspartame and sucralose.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a food preservative?
questions.explanation: Food preservatives include salt, sugar, sodium benzoate and sulphur dioxide in permitted uses.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used in non-stick coatings?
questions.explanation: Teflon is the trade name commonly used for polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), a chemically resistant, low-friction polymer used in non-stick coatings, seals and industrial applications.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used in pipes and cable insulation?
questions.explanation: PVC is polyvinyl chloride, a synthetic polymer made from vinyl chloride monomers; used in pipes, cable insulation, flooring and other products.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used in textiles, ropes and engineering components?
questions.explanation: Nylon is a family of synthetic polyamide polymers used in textiles, ropes, engineering components and fibres.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which reaction produces brown colour and characteristic flavours in cooked foods through reactions between reducing sugars and amino compounds?
questions.explanation: The Maillard reaction is a set of reactions between reducing sugars and amino compounds that produces brown colour and characteristic flavours in cooked foods.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which process involves thermal decomposition and transformation of sugars on heating?
questions.explanation: Caramelisation is the thermal decomposition and transformation of sugars on heating, producing brown-coloured compounds and characteristic flavours.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which process converts atmospheric nitrogen into biologically usable nitrogen compounds?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen fixation is the conversion of atmospheric nitrogen (N₂) into biologically usable nitrogen compounds, by nitrogen-fixing microbes, lightning or industrial processes.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which process involves microbial oxidation of ammonia to nitrite and then nitrate?
questions.explanation: Nitrification is the microbial oxidation of ammonia/ammonium to nitrite and then nitrate, mainly by specialised microorganisms.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which process involves microbial reduction of nitrate to gaseous nitrogen forms?
questions.explanation: Denitrification is the microbial reduction of nitrate or nitrite to gaseous nitrogen forms, returning nitrogen to the atmosphere, often under low-oxygen conditions.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which method is used to extract highly reactive metals such as sodium?
questions.explanation: Highly reactive metals such as sodium are extracted by electrolysis of suitable molten salts, because chemical reduction with carbon is generally unsuitable.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which method is commonly used to extract moderately reactive metals such as iron?

options.B: Reduction of oxides using carbon or carbon monoxide

questions.explanation: Moderately reactive metals such as iron are commonly extracted by reducing their oxides using carbon or carbon monoxide in a furnace; iron is produced in a blast furnace from iron ore.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which indicator is colourless in acidic solution and pink in alkaline solution?
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acidic and approximately neutral solutions; pink to magenta in alkaline solution over its transition range.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which indicator is red in acidic solution and yellow in alkaline solution?
questions.explanation: Methyl orange is red in acidic solution, orange near its transition range and yellow in alkaline solution.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which natural indicator turns reddish-brown in alkaline conditions?
questions.explanation: Turmeric remains yellow in acidic and neutral conditions and turns reddish-brown in alkaline conditions.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which factor increases the rate of reaction by providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy?
questions.explanation: A catalyst changes the rate of a reaction by providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy and is regenerated overall; it does not change the equilibrium position.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which factor increases reaction rate because a greater fraction of particles has energy equal to or greater than the activation energy?
questions.explanation: Increasing temperature often increases reaction rate because a greater fraction of particles has energy equal to or greater than the activation energy, and effective collisions become more frequent.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which factor increases reaction rate because powder has a larger exposed surface area?
questions.explanation: Powder has a larger exposed surface area, allowing more frequent effective contact with the other reactant, thus increasing reaction rate.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of rust commonly represented as?
questions.explanation: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, commonly represented as Fe₂O₃·xH₂O.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of ozone?
questions.explanation: Ozone has the formula O₃; it is a triatomic form of oxygen.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of hydrogen peroxide?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide has the formula H₂O₂; used in some disinfecting and bleaching formulations.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of bleaching powder commonly given at school level?
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is commonly represented as calcium oxychloride, CaOCl₂, though commercial material is a mixture; used for bleaching and disinfection.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of urea?
questions.explanation: Urea has the formula CO(NH₂)₂; it is a common nitrogen fertiliser.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How many periods are in the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: There are 18 vertical groups and 7 horizontal periods in the modern periodic table.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How many groups are in the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: There are 18 vertical groups and 7 horizontal periods in the modern periodic table.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which subatomic particle has a relative charge of +1?
questions.explanation: A proton has a relative charge of +1 and a relative mass of about 1.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which subatomic particle has a relative charge of -1?
questions.explanation: An electron has a relative charge of -1 and a relative mass of about 1/1836.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which subatomic particle has no charge?
questions.explanation: A neutron has a charge of 0 and a relative mass of about 1.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which part of a soap molecule is attracted to water?
questions.explanation: Soap molecules have a hydrophilic ionic head and a hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail; the ionic head is attracted to water.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which part of a soap molecule is attracted to oily dirt?
questions.explanation: Soap molecules have a hydrophilic ionic head and a hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail; the hydrocarbon tail is attracted to oily dirt.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which method of rust prevention involves coating iron with zinc?
questions.explanation: Galvanisation is coating iron or steel with zinc to protect it from corrosion; zinc provides a barrier and can also act sacrificially if the coating is damaged.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which method of rust prevention involves depositing a thin layer of one metal on another by electrolysis?
questions.explanation: Electroplating is depositing a thin layer of one metal on another by electrolysis; it can improve appearance, corrosion resistance or surface properties.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a saturated hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Methane is a saturated hydrocarbon (alkane) containing only carbon-carbon single bonds. Ethene and propene are alkenes; ethyne is an alkyne.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an unsaturated hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Ethene is an unsaturated hydrocarbon (alkene) containing a carbon-carbon double bond. Methane, ethane and propane are saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the functional group in ethanoic acid?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid is a carboxylic acid containing the -COOH functional group.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the functional group in ethanol?
questions.explanation: Ethanol is an alcohol containing a hydroxyl group (-OH) bonded to a saturated carbon atom.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a greenhouse gas?
questions.explanation: Methane is a greenhouse gas. Major greenhouse gases include water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, ozone and fluorinated gases.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Below what pH is rain conventionally termed acid rain?
questions.explanation: Conventionally, rain below about pH 5.6 is termed acid rain.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a method to reduce water hardness?
questions.explanation: Methods to reduce water hardness include boiling for temporary hardness, washing soda treatment, ion-exchange resins and reverse osmosis.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a nitrogen fertiliser?
questions.explanation: Urea is a nitrogen fertiliser with formula CO(NH₂)₂, containing about 46% nitrogen by mass in pure form.

questions.subject: General Science

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a physical change?
questions.explanation: Melting ice is a physical change. Physical changes include melting ice, cutting paper and dissolving sugar in water. Chemical changes include rusting, combustion and curdling of milk.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Combustion is a chemical change. Chemical changes include rusting, combustion and curdling of milk.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements is a metal?
questions.explanation: Sodium is a metal. Metals are generally located on the left and centre of the periodic table; non-metals are mostly on the upper right side.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements is a non-metal?
questions.explanation: Chlorine is a non-metal. Non-metals are mostly on the upper right side of the periodic table.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an ionic compound?
questions.explanation: NaCl is an ionic compound formed by electron transfer from sodium to chlorine. H₂O, CO₂ and CH₄ are covalent compounds.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a covalent compound?
questions.explanation: CO₂ is a covalent compound. Examples of covalent compounds include water (H₂O), carbon dioxide (CO₂), methane (CH₄), ammonia (NH₃) and hydrogen chloride (HCl).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following metals reacts violently with cold water?
questions.explanation: Sodium and potassium react violently with cold water; calcium reacts less vigorously; magnesium reacts with hot water/steam; iron reacts with steam; copper, silver and gold do not react with water under ordinary conditions.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following metals does not react with water under ordinary conditions?
questions.explanation: Copper, silver and gold do not react with water under ordinary conditions.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an alcohol?
questions.explanation: C₂H₅OH (ethanol) is an alcohol containing a hydroxyl group (-OH) bonded to a saturated carbon atom.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a carboxylic acid?
questions.explanation: CH₃COOH (ethanoic acid) is a carboxylic acid containing the -COOH functional group.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an aldehyde?
questions.explanation: CH₃CHO (ethanal) is an aldehyde containing a terminal -CHO functional group.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a ketone?
questions.explanation: CH₃COCH₃ (propanone/acetone) is a ketone containing a carbonyl group (>C=O) bonded to two carbon groups.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used to relieve pain?
questions.explanation: Analgesics are medicines that relieve pain; examples include paracetamol and ibuprofen.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used to neutralise excess stomach acid?
questions.explanation: Antacids are substances that neutralise excess stomach acid; examples include magnesium hydroxide, aluminium hydroxide and calcium carbonate.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used to kill bacteria or inhibit their growth?
questions.explanation: Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria or inhibit their growth; they do not treat viral infections.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is applied to living tissue to reduce or inhibit microorganisms?
questions.explanation: Antiseptics are chemical agents applied to living tissue to reduce or inhibit microorganisms; examples include appropriately formulated povidone-iodine and chlorhexidine products.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is formed when sunlight drives reactions involving nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds?
questions.explanation: Photochemical smog is air pollution formed when sunlight drives reactions involving nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds, producing ground-level ozone and other oxidants.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is made unusually acidic mainly by sulphuric and nitric acids?
questions.explanation: Acid rain is rain or other precipitation made unusually acidic mainly by sulphuric and nitric acids formed from atmospheric SO₂ and nitrogen oxides.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet-B radiation?
questions.explanation: The ozone layer is a region of the stratosphere with relatively high ozone concentration that absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet-B radiation.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following makes Earth habitable by absorbing and re-emitting infrared radiation?
questions.explanation: The greenhouse effect is warming that occurs because greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation emitted by Earth's surface; the natural effect makes Earth habitable, while human emissions strengthen it.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used to disinfect water by inactivating disease-causing microorganisms?
questions.explanation: Chlorination of water is disinfection by adding chlorine or chlorine-releasing compounds to inactivate many disease-causing microorganisms; dosage and contact time must be controlled.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following does NOT remove dissolved salts from water?
questions.explanation: Boiling kills many pathogens but does not remove dissolved non-volatile salts; evaporation can even concentrate them. Distillation, reverse osmosis and ion-exchange can remove dissolved salts.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is produced during incomplete combustion of hydrocarbons?

options.B: Carbon monoxide, soot and other products

questions.explanation: Incomplete combustion with insufficient oxygen can produce carbon monoxide, soot and other products; carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a non-renewable fossil fuel?
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels are coal, petroleum and natural gas formed from ancient organic matter over geological time; they are non-renewable on human timescales.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a method of preventing rusting?
questions.explanation: Adding salt accelerates rusting. Rusting can be prevented by painting, oiling/greasing, plastic coating, galvanising, electroplating, alloying or using cathodic protection.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used in baking, as a mild antacid and in some fire extinguishers?
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate or sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO₃; used in baking, as a mild antacid and in some fire extinguishers.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used in washing, water softening and manufacture of glass and chemicals?
questions.explanation: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O, used in washing, water softening and manufacture of glass and chemicals.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used for bleaching and disinfection?
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is commonly represented as calcium oxychloride, CaOCl₂, though commercial material is a mixture; used for bleaching and disinfection.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used for casts, moulds and decorative work?
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO₄·½H₂O; it sets with water to form gypsum and is used for casts, moulds and decorative work.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of common salt?
questions.explanation: Common salt is sodium chloride, NaCl.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of baking soda?
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO₃.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of washing soda?
questions.explanation: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of gypsum?
questions.explanation: Gypsum is calcium sulphate dihydrate, CaSO₄·2H₂O.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of Plaster of Paris?
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO₄·½H₂O.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the main acid in vinegar?
questions.explanation: Vinegar acid is ethanoic (acetic) acid, CH₃COOH.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of urea?
questions.explanation: Urea has the formula CO(NH₂)₂; it is a common nitrogen fertiliser.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is rust commonly represented as?
questions.explanation: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, commonly represented as Fe₂O₃·xH₂O.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of ozone?
questions.explanation: Ozone has the formula O₃; it is a triatomic form of oxygen.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of hydrogen peroxide?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide has the formula H₂O₂; used in some disinfecting and bleaching formulations.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of bleaching powder commonly given at school level?
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is commonly represented as calcium oxychloride, CaOCl₂, though commercial material is a mixture; used for bleaching and disinfection.

questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol K?
questions.explanation: Potassium has the symbol K (from Latin kalium).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Na?
questions.explanation: Sodium has the symbol Na (from Latin natrium).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Fe?
questions.explanation: Iron has the symbol Fe (from Latin ferrum).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Cu?

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Ag?
questions.explanation: Silver has the symbol Ag (from Latin argentum).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Sn?
questions.explanation: Tin has the symbol Sn (from Latin stannum).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Sb?
questions.explanation: Antimony has the symbol Sb (from Latin stibium).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Au?
questions.explanation: Gold has the symbol Au (from Latin aurum).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Hg?
questions.explanation: Mercury has the symbol Hg (from Latin hydrargyrum).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Pb?
questions.explanation: Lead has the symbol Pb (from Latin plumbum).

questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for magnesium?
questions.explanation: The symbol of magnesium is Mg.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for aluminium?
questions.explanation: The symbol of aluminium is Al.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for silicon?
questions.explanation: The symbol of silicon is Si.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for phosphorus?
questions.explanation: The symbol of phosphorus is P.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for sulphur?
questions.explanation: The symbol of sulphur is S.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for chlorine?
questions.explanation: The symbol of chlorine is Cl.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for argon?
questions.explanation: The symbol of argon is Ar.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for calcium?
questions.explanation: The symbol of calcium is Ca.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for hydrogen?
questions.explanation: The symbol of hydrogen is H.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for helium?
questions.explanation: The symbol of helium is He.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for lithium?
questions.explanation: The symbol of lithium is Li.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for beryllium?
questions.explanation: The symbol of beryllium is Be.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for boron?
questions.explanation: The symbol of boron is B.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for carbon?
questions.explanation: The symbol of carbon is C.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for nitrogen?
questions.explanation: The symbol of nitrogen is N.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for oxygen?
questions.explanation: The symbol of oxygen is O.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for fluorine?
questions.explanation: The symbol of fluorine is F.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for neon?
questions.explanation: The symbol of neon is Ne.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is obtained from crude oil by fractional distillation?
questions.explanation: Petroleum products are fractions obtained from crude oil by fractional distillation, including petroleum gas, petrol, naphtha, kerosene, diesel, lubricating oils, fuel oil and bitumen.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the main component of natural gas?
questions.explanation: Natural gas is mainly composed of methane (CH₄), with smaller amounts of other hydrocarbons and possible impurities depending on the source.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is produced by saponification of fats or oils with alkali?
questions.explanation: Saponification is the hydrolysis of fats or oils with a strong alkali to produce glycerol and fatty-acid salts (soap).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following indicates organic pollution in water?
questions.explanation: High BOD often indicates organic pollution because microorganisms use dissolved oxygen to decompose organic matter.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a soil contaminant?

options.A: Heavy metals such as lead and mercury

questions.explanation: Examples of soil contaminants include heavy metals such as lead, cadmium and mercury; pesticide residues; petroleum hydrocarbons; industrial solvents and excessive fertiliser nutrients.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used to slow spoilage of food?
questions.explanation: Food preservatives are substances added to food to slow spoilage caused by microorganisms, oxidation or other reactions; examples include salt, sugar, sodium benzoate and sulphur dioxide in permitted uses.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used as a sugar substitute?
questions.explanation: Artificial sweeteners are sweet-tasting substances used as sugar substitutes, often with little or no energy at the quantities used; examples include saccharin, aspartame and sucralose.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic property of metals?
questions.explanation: Most metals are lustrous, malleable, ductile, sonorous and good conductors of heat and electricity; mercury is liquid at room temperature and some metals are brittle.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic property of non-metals?
questions.explanation: Many non-metals are dull, brittle when solid and poor conductors; important exceptions include graphite, which conducts electricity, and bromine, which is liquid at room temperature.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a reaction that absorbs heat from its surroundings?
questions.explanation: An endothermic reaction is a reaction that absorbs heat from its surroundings; examples include thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate and photosynthesis overall.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a reaction that releases heat to its surroundings?
questions.explanation: An exothermic reaction is a reaction that releases heat to its surroundings; examples include combustion and many neutralisation reactions.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a noble gas?
questions.explanation: Argon is a noble gas. Noble gases include helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a metalloid?
questions.explanation: Metalloids have properties intermediate between metals and non-metals; commonly listed examples include boron, silicon, germanium, arsenic, antimony and tellurium.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a single covalent bond?
questions.explanation: A single covalent bond is formed by sharing one pair of electrons, such as the H–H bond in H₂.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a double covalent bond?
questions.explanation: A double covalent bond is formed by sharing two pairs of electrons, such as the O=O bond in O₂.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a triple covalent bond?
questions.explanation: A triple covalent bond is formed by sharing three pairs of electrons, such as the N≡N bond in nitrogen gas.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which type of hardness is mainly caused by dissolved calcium and magnesium hydrogencarbonates?
questions.explanation: Temporary hardness of water is mainly caused by dissolved calcium and magnesium hydrogencarbonates; boiling can remove much of it by precipitating insoluble compounds.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which type of hardness is mainly due to dissolved calcium and magnesium chlorides and sulphates?
questions.explanation: Permanent hardness of water is mainly due to dissolved calcium and magnesium chlorides and sulphates; it is not removed by ordinary boiling.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an ozone-depleting substance?
questions.explanation: Ozone-depleting substances such as chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and halons release chlorine or bromine radicals in the stratosphere that catalytically destroy ozone.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following gases is NOT a major greenhouse gas?
questions.explanation: Major greenhouse gases include water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, ozone and fluorinated gases. Nitrogen is not a greenhouse gas.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a homologous series?
questions.explanation: Alkanes are a homologous series of saturated open-chain hydrocarbons with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which separation technique uses a fractionating column?
questions.explanation: Fractional distillation is a distillation technique using a fractionating column to separate miscible liquids with relatively close boiling points.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following compounds is held together by ionic bonds?
questions.explanation: NaCl is an ionic compound; ionic bonds are electrostatic attractions between oppositely charged ions formed after electron transfer.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a strong acid?
questions.explanation: HCl is a strong acid. Examples of strong acids include hydrochloric acid (HCl), nitric acid (HNO₃) and sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a weak acid?
questions.explanation: CH₃COOH (ethanoic acid) is a weak acid. Examples of weak acids include ethanoic acid, carbonic acid and citric acid.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a strong base?
questions.explanation: NaOH is a strong base. Examples of strong bases include sodium hydroxide (NaOH), potassium hydroxide (KOH) and barium hydroxide [Ba(OH)₂].

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an antibiotic?
questions.explanation: Penicillin is an antibiotic. Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria or inhibit their growth; they do not treat viral infections.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an analgesic?
questions.explanation: Paracetamol is an analgesic. Analgesics are medicines that relieve pain; examples include paracetamol and ibuprofen.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an antacid?
questions.explanation: Magnesium hydroxide is an antacid. Antacids are substances that neutralise excess stomach acid; examples include magnesium hydroxide, aluminium hydroxide and calcium carbonate.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an antiseptic?
questions.explanation: Povidone-iodine is an antiseptic. Antiseptics are chemical agents applied to living tissue to reduce or inhibit microorganisms.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following causes eutrophication?
questions.explanation: Eutrophication is excess nutrient enrichment, especially by nitrogen and phosphorus, causing algal blooms and oxygen depletion that can harm aquatic life.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a natural polymer?
questions.explanation: Cellulose is a natural polymer. Natural polymers include cellulose, starch, proteins, natural rubber and DNA.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a synthetic polymer?
questions.explanation: Nylon is a synthetic polymer. Synthetic polymers are human-made polymers produced by chemical processes; examples include nylon, polyethylene, PVC and polyester.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a thermoplastic?
questions.explanation: Thermoplastics soften on heating and can generally be remoulded; polyethylene is a thermoplastic. Thermosetting plastics such as Bakelite form cross-linked networks and do not melt and remould easily.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a thermosetting plastic?
questions.explanation: Thermosetting plastics form cross-linked networks and do not melt and remould easily after curing; Bakelite is a common example.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used to disinfect water?
questions.explanation: Chlorination of water is disinfection by adding chlorine or chlorine-releasing compounds to inactivate many disease-causing microorganisms.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a method of preventing rusting by coating iron with zinc?
questions.explanation: Galvanisation is coating iron or steel with zinc to protect it from corrosion; zinc provides a barrier and can also act sacrificially if the coating is damaged.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a saturated hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Methane is a saturated hydrocarbon (alkane) containing only carbon-carbon single bonds.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an unsaturated hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Ethene is an unsaturated hydrocarbon (alkene) containing a carbon-carbon double bond.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following produces brown colour and characteristic flavours in cooked foods through reactions between reducing sugars and amino compounds?
questions.explanation: The Maillard reaction is a set of reactions between reducing sugars and amino compounds that produces brown colour and characteristic flavours in cooked foods.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following involves thermal decomposition and transformation of sugars on heating?
questions.explanation: Caramelisation is the thermal decomposition and transformation of sugars on heating, producing brown-coloured compounds and characteristic flavours.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which process converts atmospheric nitrogen into biologically usable nitrogen compounds?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen fixation is the conversion of atmospheric nitrogen (N₂) into biologically usable nitrogen compounds, by nitrogen-fixing microbes, lightning or industrial processes.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which process involves microbial oxidation of ammonia to nitrite and then nitrate?
questions.explanation: Nitrification is the microbial oxidation of ammonia/ammonium to nitrite and then nitrate, mainly by specialised microorganisms.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which process involves microbial reduction of nitrate to gaseous nitrogen forms?
questions.explanation: Denitrification is the microbial reduction of nitrate or nitrite to gaseous nitrogen forms, returning nitrogen to the atmosphere, often under low-oxygen conditions.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which method is used to extract highly reactive metals such as sodium?
questions.explanation: Highly reactive metals such as sodium are extracted by electrolysis of suitable molten salts, because chemical reduction with carbon is generally unsuitable.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which method is commonly used to extract moderately reactive metals such as iron?

options.B: Reduction of oxides using carbon or carbon monoxide

questions.explanation: Moderately reactive metals such as iron are commonly extracted by reducing their oxides using carbon or carbon monoxide in a furnace; iron is produced in a blast furnace from iron ore.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which indicator is colourless in acidic solution and pink in alkaline solution?
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acidic and approximately neutral solutions; pink to magenta in alkaline solution over its transition range.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which indicator is red in acidic solution and yellow in alkaline solution?
questions.explanation: Methyl orange is red in acidic solution, orange near its transition range and yellow in alkaline solution.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which natural indicator turns reddish-brown in alkaline conditions?
questions.explanation: Turmeric remains yellow in acidic and neutral conditions and turns reddish-brown in alkaline conditions.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which factor increases the rate of reaction by providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy?
questions.explanation: A catalyst changes the rate of a reaction by providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy and is regenerated overall; it does not change the equilibrium position.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which factor increases reaction rate because a greater fraction of particles has energy equal to or greater than the activation energy?
questions.explanation: Increasing temperature often increases reaction rate because a greater fraction of particles has energy equal to or greater than the activation energy, and effective collisions become more frequent.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which factor increases reaction rate because powder has a larger exposed surface area?
questions.explanation: Powder has a larger exposed surface area, allowing more frequent effective contact with the other reactant, thus increasing reaction rate.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of rust commonly represented as?
questions.explanation: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, commonly represented as Fe₂O₃·xH₂O.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of ozone?
questions.explanation: Ozone has the formula O₃; it is a triatomic form of oxygen.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of hydrogen peroxide?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide has the formula H₂O₂; used in some disinfecting and bleaching formulations.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of bleaching powder commonly given at school level?
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is commonly represented as calcium oxychloride, CaOCl₂, though commercial material is a mixture; used for bleaching and disinfection.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of urea?
questions.explanation: Urea has the formula CO(NH₂)₂; it is a common nitrogen fertiliser.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How many periods are in the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: There are 18 vertical groups and 7 horizontal periods in the modern periodic table.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: How many groups are in the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: There are 18 vertical groups and 7 horizontal periods in the modern periodic table.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which subatomic particle has a relative charge of +1?
questions.explanation: A proton has a relative charge of +1 and a relative mass of about 1.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which subatomic particle has a relative charge of -1?
questions.explanation: An electron has a relative charge of -1 and a relative mass of about 1/1836.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which subatomic particle has no charge?
questions.explanation: A neutron has a charge of 0 and a relative mass of about 1.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which part of a soap molecule is attracted to water?
questions.explanation: Soap molecules have a hydrophilic ionic head and a hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail; the ionic head is attracted to water.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which part of a soap molecule is attracted to oily dirt?
questions.explanation: Soap molecules have a hydrophilic ionic head and a hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail; the hydrocarbon tail is attracted to oily dirt.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which method of rust prevention involves coating iron with zinc?
questions.explanation: Galvanisation is coating iron or steel with zinc to protect it from corrosion; zinc provides a barrier and can also act sacrificially if the coating is damaged.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which method of rust prevention involves depositing a thin layer of one metal on another by electrolysis?
questions.explanation: Electroplating is depositing a thin layer of one metal on another by electrolysis; it can improve appearance, corrosion resistance or surface properties.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a saturated hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Methane is a saturated hydrocarbon (alkane) containing only carbon-carbon single bonds.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an unsaturated hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Ethene is an unsaturated hydrocarbon (alkene) containing a carbon-carbon double bond.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the functional group in ethanoic acid?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid is a carboxylic acid containing the -COOH functional group.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the functional group in ethanol?
questions.explanation: Ethanol is an alcohol containing a hydroxyl group (-OH) bonded to a saturated carbon atom.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a greenhouse gas?
questions.explanation: Methane is a greenhouse gas. Major greenhouse gases include water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, ozone and fluorinated gases.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Below what pH is rain conventionally termed acid rain?
questions.explanation: Conventionally, rain below about pH 5.6 is termed acid rain.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a method to reduce water hardness?
questions.explanation: Methods to reduce water hardness include boiling for temporary hardness, washing soda treatment, ion-exchange resins and reverse osmosis.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a nitrogen fertiliser?
questions.explanation: Urea is a nitrogen fertiliser with formula CO(NH₂)₂, containing about 46% nitrogen by mass in pure form.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used to control insects?
questions.explanation: An insecticide is a pesticide used to control insects.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used to control weeds?
questions.explanation: A herbicide is a pesticide used to control unwanted plants or weeds.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used to control fungal diseases?
questions.explanation: A fungicide is a pesticide used to prevent or control fungal diseases.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a physical change?
questions.explanation: Melting ice is a physical change. Physical changes include melting ice, cutting paper and dissolving sugar in water.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Combustion is a chemical change. Chemical changes include rusting, combustion and curdling of milk.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements is a metal?
questions.explanation: Sodium is a metal. Metals are generally located on the left and centre of the periodic table.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements is a non-metal?
questions.explanation: Chlorine is a non-metal. Non-metals are mostly on the upper right side of the periodic table.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an ionic compound?
questions.explanation: NaCl is an ionic compound formed by electron transfer from sodium to chlorine. H₂O, CO₂ and CH₄ are covalent compounds.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a covalent compound?
questions.explanation: CO₂ is a covalent compound. Examples of covalent compounds include water (H₂O), carbon dioxide (CO₂), methane (CH₄), ammonia (NH₃) and hydrogen chloride (HCl).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following metals reacts violently with cold water?
questions.explanation: Sodium and potassium react violently with cold water; calcium reacts less vigorously; magnesium reacts with hot water/steam; iron reacts with steam; copper, silver and gold do not react with water under ordinary conditions.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following metals does not react with water under ordinary conditions?
questions.explanation: Copper, silver and gold do not react with water under ordinary conditions.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an alcohol?
questions.explanation: C₂H₅OH (ethanol) is an alcohol containing a hydroxyl group (-OH) bonded to a saturated carbon atom.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a carboxylic acid?
questions.explanation: CH₃COOH (ethanoic acid) is a carboxylic acid containing the -COOH functional group.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is an aldehyde?
questions.explanation: CH₃CHO (ethanal) is an aldehyde containing a terminal -CHO functional group.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a ketone?
questions.explanation: CH₃COCH₃ (propanone/acetone) is a ketone containing a carbonyl group (>C=O) bonded to two carbon groups.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used to relieve pain?
questions.explanation: Analgesics are medicines that relieve pain; examples include paracetamol and ibuprofen.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used to neutralise excess stomach acid?
questions.explanation: Antacids are substances that neutralise excess stomach acid; examples include magnesium hydroxide, aluminium hydroxide and calcium carbonate.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used to kill bacteria or inhibit their growth?
questions.explanation: Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria or inhibit their growth; they do not treat viral infections.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is applied to living tissue to reduce or inhibit microorganisms?
questions.explanation: Antiseptics are chemical agents applied to living tissue to reduce or inhibit microorganisms; examples include appropriately formulated povidone-iodine and chlorhexidine products.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is formed when sunlight drives reactions involving nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds?
questions.explanation: Photochemical smog is air pollution formed when sunlight drives reactions involving nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds, producing ground-level ozone and other oxidants.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is made unusually acidic mainly by sulphuric and nitric acids?
questions.explanation: Acid rain is rain or other precipitation made unusually acidic mainly by sulphuric and nitric acids formed from atmospheric SO₂ and nitrogen oxides.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet-B radiation?
questions.explanation: The ozone layer is a region of the stratosphere with relatively high ozone concentration that absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet-B radiation.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following makes Earth habitable by absorbing and re-emitting infrared radiation?
questions.explanation: The greenhouse effect is warming that occurs because greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation emitted by Earth's surface; the natural effect makes Earth habitable, while human emissions strengthen it.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used to disinfect water by inactivating disease-causing microorganisms?
questions.explanation: Chlorination of water is disinfection by adding chlorine or chlorine-releasing compounds to inactivate many disease-causing microorganisms; dosage and contact time must be controlled.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following does NOT remove dissolved salts from water?
questions.explanation: Boiling kills many pathogens but does not remove dissolved non-volatile salts; evaporation can even concentrate them. Distillation, reverse osmosis and ion-exchange can remove dissolved salts.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is produced during incomplete combustion of hydrocarbons?

options.B: Carbon monoxide, soot and other products

questions.explanation: Incomplete combustion with insufficient oxygen can produce carbon monoxide, soot and other products; carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a non-renewable fossil fuel?
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels are coal, petroleum and natural gas formed from ancient organic matter over geological time; they are non-renewable on human timescales.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a method of preventing rusting?
questions.explanation: Adding salt accelerates rusting. Rusting can be prevented by painting, oiling/greasing, plastic coating, galvanising, electroplating, alloying or using cathodic protection.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used in baking, as a mild antacid and in some fire extinguishers?
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate or sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO₃; used in baking, as a mild antacid and in some fire extinguishers.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used in washing, water softening and manufacture of glass and chemicals?
questions.explanation: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O, used in washing, water softening and manufacture of glass and chemicals.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used for bleaching and disinfection?
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is commonly represented as calcium oxychloride, CaOCl₂, though commercial material is a mixture; used for bleaching and disinfection.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is used for casts, moulds and decorative work?
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO₄·½H₂O; it sets with water to form gypsum and is used for casts, moulds and decorative work.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of common salt?
questions.explanation: Common salt is sodium chloride, NaCl.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of baking soda?
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO₃.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of washing soda?
questions.explanation: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of gypsum?
questions.explanation: Gypsum is calcium sulphate dihydrate, CaSO₄·2H₂O.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of Plaster of Paris?
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO₄·½H₂O.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the main acid in vinegar?
questions.explanation: Vinegar acid is ethanoic (acetic) acid, CH₃COOH.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of urea?
questions.explanation: Urea has the formula CO(NH₂)₂; it is a common nitrogen fertiliser.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is rust commonly represented as?
questions.explanation: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, commonly represented as Fe₂O₃·xH₂O.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of ozone?
questions.explanation: Ozone has the formula O₃; it is a triatomic form of oxygen.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of hydrogen peroxide?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide has the formula H₂O₂; used in some disinfecting and bleaching formulations.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of bleaching powder commonly given at school level?
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is commonly represented as calcium oxychloride, CaOCl₂, though commercial material is a mixture; used for bleaching and disinfection.

questions.explanation: Potassium has the symbol K (from Latin kalium).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Na?
questions.explanation: Sodium has the symbol Na (from Latin natrium).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Fe?
questions.explanation: Iron has the symbol Fe (from Latin ferrum).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Cu?
questions.explanation: Copper has the symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Ag?
questions.explanation: Silver has the symbol Ag (from Latin argentum).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Sn?
questions.explanation: Tin has the symbol Sn (from Latin stannum).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Sb?
questions.explanation: Antimony has the symbol Sb (from Latin stibium).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Au?
questions.explanation: Gold has the symbol Au (from Latin aurum).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Hg?
questions.explanation: Mercury has the symbol Hg (from Latin hydrargyrum).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following elements has the symbol Pb?
questions.explanation: Lead has the symbol Pb (from Latin plumbum).

questions.explanation: The symbol of magnesium is Mg.

questions.explanation: The symbol of aluminium is Al.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for silicon?
questions.explanation: The symbol of silicon is Si.

questions.subject: General Science

questions.explanation: The symbol of phosphorus is P.

questions.explanation: The symbol of sulphur is S.

questions.question: Which of the following is the symbol for calcium?
questions.explanation: The symbol of calcium is Ca.
